summary: Gavin Flood is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Lancaster University under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith. He held professorships at the University of Stirling and the University of Oxford, where he also directed the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies.

Gelek is a Tibetology scholar who served as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center, attested in 1998. He has also held appointments as a visiting lecturer at the University of California and as a visiting scholar at the University of Oxford.

Gelek Rinpoche was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery, the Young Lamas Home School, and Cornell University under several traditional teachers. He served as director of Tibet House, New Delhi, and founded Jewel Heart in 1988.

Gembo Dorji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed studies at Tango Buddhist College, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo, and trained under several traditional teachers, including Tenzin Dhendrup and Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima.

Gen'ichi Yamazaki was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He worked as a full-time researcher at Toyo Bunko from circa 1964 to 1981 and served as a professor at Kokugakuin University in 2006.

Genchi Kato was a scholar of religious studies and Japanology who studied under Tetsujiro Inoue at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships with the Imperial Japanese Army and taught at the University of Tokyo, Kokugakuin University, and Taisho University.

Gendun Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master who founded Dhagpo Kagyu Ling, Dhagpo Kundreul Ling, and Dhagpo Dedrol Ling. From circa 1977 to 1997, he served as the abbot and retreat master at Dhagpo Kagyu Ling.

Gendün Chöphel was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Drisha, Kumbum, Labrang, and Drepung monasteries, training under Gendun Tendzin Gyatso and Sherab Gyatso, and was affiliated with the Maha Bodhi Society in 1941.

Genjun Sasaki was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who graduated from Kyoto University and studied under several scholars, including Tokuryu Yamauchi. He was a professor at Otani University and held visiting positions at Harvard University and the University of Hamburg.
Genro Gito was an 18th-century Buddhist studies figure who succeeded Hakuin Ekaku. He served as the first seat (dai-ichiza) at Myōshin-ji.
Genryu Kagoshima was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from circa 1931 to 1937. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University from circa 1960 to 1983.

Gensho Imanari was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from Waseda University. He was an assistant professor at Kokushikan University before becoming a professor and later professor emeritus at Rissho University.
Genshu Watanabe was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Toyo University. He trained as a dharma heir under Sogaku Daiun Harada.

Genta Ikeda was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University and became a professor emeritus at Nara University of Education around 1965.
Genzao was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950 and trained under traditional teachers Jiangze Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche.

Geo Widengren was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies. Educated at Stockholm and Uppsala universities under Henrik Samuel Nyberg, he was Professor of the History of Religions at Uppsala University (1940–1973) and president of the IAHR.

Geoff Childs is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who completed his PhD at Indiana University, where he studied under Tsetan Chonjore. He held positions at the Australian National University and Washington University in St. Louis.

Geoffrey Barstow is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche and earned degrees from Hampshire College, Kathmandu University, and the University of Virginia, later becoming an assistant professor at Oregon State University.

Geoffrey Goble is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned an MA at the University of Virginia and a PhD at Indiana University, later serving as an assistant professor of religious studies at the University of Oklahoma.

Geoffrey Samuel is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Cambridge under Edmund Leach, Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, and Peter J. Wilson. He held professorships at Lancaster University, Newcastle, and Cardiff University.
